title: libimage: report the size a removal actually frees
body:
Fixes: https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/27592

`report.Size` is the image's full size — `i.Size()` is `store.ImageSize()`, which counts every layer including the shared ones. podman sums those reports, so a layer shared by N pruned images is counted N times. Users saw "reclaimed 346GB" on a 128GB disk.

This adds `RemoveImageReport.FreedSize`, the number of bytes the removal released. `Size` keeps its current meaning, so existing callers are unaffected.

c/storage already walks the layer chain and stops at the first layer another image still references, so `DeleteImageWithSize` reuses that walk and sums the layers it is about to remove, under the same lock that removes them. No second walk, no dry run, and no window in which a concurrent removal could skew the number. A layer shared by several removed images is released when the last of them goes, so it is accounted exactly once and summing `FreedSize` over a removal gives the space it released.

Layers are measured uncompressed, the same metric `DiskUsage` uses, so the number stays comparable with what `podman system df` reports.

Tests: two images sharing a top layer are removed together; the summed `FreedSize` equals the disk usage measured before the removal, and `sum(Size)` is strictly greater. Reverting the accounting reports 11692362 against an actual 5848394.

Podman needs a vendor bump and a switch from `r.Size` to `r.FreedSize` in `pkg/domain/infra/abi/images.go`; PR to follow, with the bump as its own commit.
